```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = NA, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.2)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(sf)
  library(tmap)
  library(VancouvR)
})
```

## An sf object is a table with a geometry column

```{r}
#| label: parks
parks <- st_read("data/Park_Inventory.geojson", quiet = TRUE)
parks |> select(NAME, CLASSIFICATION) |> head(3)
```

The `geometry` column holds each park's boundary. It stays attached through `select()` and `filter()`.

## Read spatial files with st_read()

- **GeoJSON**: one file, such as `data/Park_Inventory.geojson`.
- **Shapefile**: several files with the same name (`.shp`, `.shx`, `.dbf`, `.prj`, …). Keep them together and read the `.shp`.

```{r}
#| label: shp
parks_shp <- st_read("data/Park_Inventory/Park_Inventory.shp", quiet = TRUE)
nrow(parks) == nrow(parks_shp)
```

## Open data portals publish spatial data

- [City of Vancouver Open Data](https://opendata.vancouver.ca/)
- [Burnaby Open Data](https://data.burnaby.ca/)
- [DataBC](https://www.data.gov.bc.ca/)

For Vancouver, `VancouvR` downloads a dataset by its identifier:

```{r}
#| label: cov
stations <- get_cov_data("rapid-transit-stations") |> select(station)
zoning <- get_cov_data("zoning-districts-and-labels") |>
  select(zoning_classification)
```

## Turn coordinates into points

```{r}
#| label: sales
bca <- read_rds("data/bca262.rds")

sales <- bca |>
  filter(year(sale_date) == 2023, juris_label == "City of Vancouver",
         !is.na(lon), !is.na(lat)) |>
  select(folioid, sale_date, price, lon, lat) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
nrow(sales)
```

`crs = 4326` says that the coordinates are longitude and latitude.

## A coordinate reference system gives coordinates meaning

| EPSG code | Name | Units | Use it for |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4326 | WGS 84 | degrees | Longitude and latitude, from GPS or most web data |
| 32610 | UTM zone 10N | metres | Distances and buffers in BC |
| 3347 | Statistics Canada Lambert | metres | Maps of all of Canada or several provinces |

```{r}
#| label: crs
st_crs(sales)$epsg
st_crs(stations)$epsg
```

## A wrong CRS puts points in the wrong place

VPD crime data store `X` and `Y` in **UTM metres**, not degrees:

```{r}
#| label: crimes-wrong
vpd_file <- file.path("data", "crimedata_csv_AllNeighbourhoods_2026",
                      "crimedata_csv_AllNeighbourhoods_2026.csv")
crimes <- read_csv(vpd_file) |>
  filter(X != 0, Y != 0)   # 0 means the location was withheld

st_as_sf(crimes, coords = c("X", "Y"), crs = 4326) |> st_bbox()
```

A "latitude" of 5 million is impossible. R created the object anyway.

## Declare the CRS the data actually use

```{r}
#| label: crimes-right
crimes_sf <- st_as_sf(crimes, coords = c("X", "Y"), crs = 32610)
crimes_sf |> st_transform(4326) |> st_bbox() |> round(3)
```

::: {.key-point}
Read the data's documentation for its CRS. Never guess.
:::

## A spatial join attaches the polygon each point falls in

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| label: zoning-join
sales_zoning <- sales |> st_join(zoning)
c(before = nrow(sales), after = nrow(sales_zoning))

sales_zoning |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(zoning_classification, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(4)
```
:::

Both layers must use the same CRS. Check with `st_crs()`.

## Map the result to check it

```{r}
#| label: zoning-map
#| fig-height: 4
tm_shape(zoning) + tm_polygons(fill = "grey95", col = "grey70") +
  tm_shape(sales_zoning) + tm_dots(fill = "zoning_classification", size = 0.2)
```

::: {.notes}
In class, switch to `tmap_mode("view")` and click points near zoning boundaries to check the join.
:::

## Buffers need metres

```{r}
#| label: buffer
stations_300 <- stations |>
  st_transform(32610) |>
  st_buffer(300)

sales_near <- sales |>
  st_transform(32610) |>
  st_join(stations_300)
```

`st_buffer(300)` draws a 300-unit circle. In EPSG 32610 that is 300 metres.

## Overlapping buffers duplicate rows

```{r}
#| label: dup
nrow(sales)
nrow(sales_near)
```

::: {.warning}
A sale within 300 m of two stations matches both, so it appears twice. Counts per station are fine, but totals and averages across all sales double-count these rows.
:::

## Count sales near each station

```{r}
#| label: count
sales_near |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(!is.na(station)) |>
  count(station, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(5)
```

Without `filter(!is.na(station))`, sales near no station would appear as an `NA` row.

## Practice: crimes near stations

Count the crimes within 500 m of each rapid transit station.

1. Use `crimes_sf` (EPSG 32610) and `stations`.
2. Put both layers in EPSG 32610 and buffer the stations by 500 m.
3. Check the row count before and after the join.

## Answer

::: {.small}
```{r include=params$answers}
#| label: practice
stations_500 <- stations |> st_transform(32610) |> st_buffer(500)
crimes_near <- crimes_sf |> st_join(stations_500)
c(before = nrow(crimes_sf), after = nrow(crimes_near))

crimes_near |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(!is.na(station)) |>
  count(station, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(5)
```
:::
